rows.file: J032_A5_alphavantage.mp4 · 1920×1080 · up to 60s (sped up in the edit) · plus J032_A5_answer.png
rows.how: **Setup, off camera:** get a free key at https://www.alphavantage.co/support/#api-key (don't film this page). Save the key in Bitwarden. **Film:** 1. Start recording. Chrome → https://claude.ai/customize/connectors → browse the directory → type `Alpha Vantage` in the search. 2. Click the Alpha Vantage tile → Connect. 3. **Stop recording** while the key is entered. Start again once it shows Connected; hold 2s. 4. New chat. Type exactly, don't paste: `Use Alpha Vantage. What's Apple's latest price, what did it report in its last earnings, and what's the news on Apple this week?` Press Enter. 5. When "Claude wants to use … from Alpha Vantage" appears, hold 1s, then click **Allow once** (every time it asks). 6. Keep recording until the answer is finished. Scroll it slowly top to bottom in about 4s. 7. Screenshot the answer (J032_A5_answer.png). **CHECK: the answer must come from Alpha Vantage (its tool calls show in the chat).** If Claude answers without using it, start a new chat and run step 4 again. **CHECK: if the answer says buy, sell or hold, crop that part out or run it again adding `Just the facts, no opinion.` at the end.**
rows.what: Alpha Vantage: add it, ask, allow, answer

rows.file: J032_A6_coingecko.mp4 · 1920×1080 · up to 60s (sped up) · plus J032_A6_table.png
rows.how: 1. Start recording. https://claude.ai/customize/connectors → **Add custom connector**. 2. Name: `CoinGecko`. URL: `https://mcp.api.coingecko.com/mcp`. Click Add, then Connect. Hold 2s on Connected. **CHECK: if that URL fails, use the free public server URL on https://docs.coingecko.com/docs/mcp-server and tell Mark which one worked.** 3. New chat. Type exactly: `Use CoinGecko. What's trending in crypto right now? Then compare Bitcoin, Ethereum and Solana in a table: price, 24h volume and market cap.` Press Enter. 4. Hold 1s on "Claude wants to use … from CoinGecko", then **Allow once** (every time it asks). 5. Keep recording until the table is finished. Hold 3s on the table. 6. Screenshot the table (J032_A6_table.png). **CHECK: the table has all three coins and all three columns. If not, run step 3 again in a new chat.**
rows.what: CoinGecko: add it, compare three coins

rows.file: J032_A7_qube.mp4 · 1920×1080 · up to 3 min (sped up) · plus the 4 PNGs
rows.how: 1. Terminal, dark theme, font size 22, full screen. Start recording. 2. Type `claude`, press Enter. Hold 2s on the screen that shows Qube is connected. 3. Type exactly, don't paste: `Build this strategy in Qube and backtest it: buy Microsoft (MSFT) when its 20-day moving average crosses above its 50-day moving average. Sell when it crosses back below. Start with $10,000. Test it from Jan 2021 to Dec 2025. Show me every trade and flag the weak spots.` Press Enter. 4. When Claude asks permission to use Qube, hold 1s, then choose **Yes**. 5. Keep recording until the backtest result is shown. Then open the same run in Qube in Chrome and record: the result screen (hold 3s), the full trade list scrolled top to bottom in about 3s, stopping where at least 3 red losing trades are on screen together (hold 3s), and the weak spots Qube flagged (hold 3s). 6. Back in the terminal, type exactly: `Now optimize it, then backtest the optimized version on the same dates.` Press Enter, allow, and record until the optimized result is shown. Open it in Qube and hold 3s on the result. 7. Screenshots: J032_A7_result_before.png, J032_A7_trades.png, J032_A7_weakspots.png, J032_A7_result_after.png. 8. Write down from the screen, for both runs: final value, number of trades, worst drop. Send the four screenshots and the numbers to Mark and the editor. **CHECK: never change a number, and don't rerun to get a better one. Whatever the first optimized result is, that's the one we show.** **CHECK: line 9 says Qube fixes the weak spots. If the optimized version doesn't beat the first one on the weakness Qube flagged (compare the two screenshots), stop and tell Mark before the edit. Don't rerun.** **CHECK: the trade list must show real losing trades in red.** **CHECK: if Qube can't build or test this strategy, stop and tell Mark; don't swap in another one.**
rows.what: Qube in Claude: type the strategy, backtest, every trade, weak spots, optimized

rows.file: J032_A8_notion.mp4 · 1920×1080 · up to 60s (sped up) · plus J032_A8_page.png
rows.how: **Setup, off camera:** 1. In Notion, make a new empty page called `Trading journal`. 2. https://claude.ai/customize/connectors → directory → search `Notion` → Connect → on Notion's page, pick the workspace and allow access to the `Trading journal` page. Don't film the workspace picker. **Film:** 3. Start recording with the empty `Trading journal` page open in Notion; hold 2s. 4. Go back to the same Claude session as A7 (Notion must show in its tools). Type exactly: `Log that test in my Trading journal page in Notion: the strategy, both backtest results, and what to try next.` Press Enter. 5. Allow the Notion permission when asked (hold 1s on it first). 6. Switch to Notion and record the page with what Claude wrote. Scroll it slowly in about 3s. Screenshot it (J032_A8_page.png). **CHECK: if Notion isn't available in the A7 session, use the fallback:** claude.ai → new chat → attach J032_A7_result_before.png and J032_A7_result_after.png → type the same prompt as step 4. Tell the editor which way was used. **CHECK: the numbers on the Notion page must match A7's screenshots. If Claude wrote a different number, stop and tell Mark; don't edit the page.**
rows.what: Notion: "Log that test" fills the journal

rows.file: J032_A9_byhand.mp4 · J032_A9_claude.mp4 · J032_A9_readback.mp4 · 1920×1080 · plus J032_A9_calendar.png and a note with both times, the save times and the 10 dates
rows.how: **The watchlist (on screen only, never spoken):** AAPL, MSFT, NVDA, AMZN, GOOGL, META, TSLA, AVGO, JPM, NFLX. **Setup, off camera:** 1. https://claude.ai/customize/connectors → find **Google Calendar** → Connect → sign in to Joshua's Google account (never film the account picker). It's read-only: it's used only for the read-back in step 14. 2. In Google Calendar, make two new calendars (gear → Settings → Add calendar → Create new calendar, https://calendar.google.com/calendar/r/settings/createcalendar): `Earnings by hand` and `Earnings from Claude`. 3. In Claude, check that file creation is on: https://claude.ai/settings → Capabilities → code execution and file creation on. 4. Mac Clock app → Stopwatch, set to 0:00, window small in the top-right corner of the screen so it's inside every recording. **By hand (film all of it, one take):** 5. Start the screen recording, then start the stopwatch. 6. For each stock in the order above: open `https://www.nasdaq.com/market-activity/stocks/aapl/earnings` (swap `aapl` for each ticker in lowercase: msft, nvda, amzn, googl, meta, tsla, avgo, jpm, nflx), find the next earnings date, then in Google Calendar make an all-day event on that date in the `Earnings by hand` calendar, called `AAPL earnings` (`MSFT earnings` and so on). Save it. 7. Stop the stopwatch the moment the 10th event is saved. Hold 3s on the stopwatch. 8. Write down the stopwatch time, the time each event was saved (from the recording) and the 10 dates. **With Claude (film all of it, one take, the stopwatch runs through the import):** 9. In Google Calendar, untick `Earnings by hand` so those events are hidden. Reset the stopwatch to 0:00. 10. claude.ai → new chat (web search off). Type the prompt below, then start the recording and the stopwatch together and press Enter: `Use Alpha Vantage to find the next earnings date for AAPL, MSFT, NVDA, AMZN, GOOGL, META, TSLA, AVGO, JPM and NFLX. Show them in a table, then make me one .ics calendar file with each date as an all-day event called "AAPL earnings", "MSFT earnings" and so on.` 11. Click **Allow once** each time Claude asks. When the file is ready, click its download button (it saves to Downloads). 12. Google Calendar → gear → Settings → Import & export (https://calendar.google.com/calendar/r/settings/export) → **Select file from your computer** → pick the .ics file from Downloads → **Add to calendar:** `Earnings from Claude` → **Import**. 13. Go to the month view. Stop the stopwatch the moment all 10 events show. Hold 3s on the stopwatch, then 3s on the calendar (two months one after the other if the dates spread out). Screenshot it (J032_A9_calendar.png). **Read-back (separate clip, not timed, in the main cut under line 15):** 14. In the same Claude chat, + → Connectors → turn on Google Calendar, then type exactly: `Which earnings events are on my Google Calendar in the next three months?` Allow once. Record the answer listing the 10 events. **CHECK: 10 events, and every date matches the date found by hand in step 6. If any is different or missing, stop and tell Mark. Don't fix it in the calendar, the file or the edit.** **CHECK: both stopwatch times are the real ones, and the Claude clock includes the download and the import. Never stop the clock early, pause it, or restart a run to get a better time.** **CHECK: if Claude can't make the .ics file, stop and tell Mark.**
rows.what: The race: 10 earnings dates by hand, then one prompt and a calendar file

notes: **Recreating:** @david_knowsai · https://www.instagram.com/p/DesH3mKRmC4/ · copy its rhythm: 28 cuts in 54s (one about every 1.9s), the screen recording itself changing every 1–2s inside a shot; all five names on screen by 2s; a full-face "#N" punch-in before every item; the "Claude wants to use…" → "Allow once" prompt visible in every demo; each demo ending on a concrete result; a running stopwatch as the payoff picture, then the Google Calendar read-back right before the CTA. **Layout:** split screen for the demos, like the original: screen recording in the top half (1080×960), Joshua in the bottom half. Full face for every "#N" label. On-screen text: Inter Bold 48px, white on #0B0F14 at 85%.
**Times** are estimates at Joshua's pace (3.2 words a second, each "#N" label held about 1.4s). Re-time to the real take.

lines.text: Here are the five most powerful Claude connectors.
Number one is perplexity.
This gives Claude access to the most powerful research engine on the planet.
So you can run deep research on any topic and pull real-time information from the entire internet.
Number two is fire crawl.
This lets Claude see the internet.
So it can scrape and copy any website, pull entire brand assets, and even do competitor research for you instantly.
Number three is post hog.
It turns Claude into your private investigator.
It uncovers bugs, finds where you're losing customers, and even automatically upgrades your website.
Number four is playwright.
This gives Claude hands so it can control your browser, fill out forms, test websites, and even use tools that don't have an AI connection.
Number five is composio.
This lets Claude connect to every app you use at once.
So instead of wasting your time installing apps one by one, you get all of them connected in one shot.
If you want the prompt to set all these up at once, just comment post and I'll shoot it over.
